description: Single-panel schematic (no micrograph) plotting true stress (MPa, vertical arrow) against true strain (horizontal arrow) to define flow-stress evolution under varying deformation conditions. A dashed vertical line at ε_I splits the strain axis into "Stage I / Before variation" and "Stage II / After variation". A four-entry legend defines: black dashed = "Constant Z_p1"; blue solid = "Decreasing Z_p from Z_p2 to Z_p1 at ε_I"; purple dashed = "Constant Z_p2"; magenta solid = "Increasing Z_p from Z_p1 to Z_p2 at ε_I". In Stage I the four curves run as two superimposed pairs rising from the initial stresses σ_01 (Z_p1 pair: black dashed + magenta) and σ_02 (Z_p2 pair: purple dashed + blue); circles mark the critical stresses σ_c1 and σ_c2 and the peak σ_p2, joined by dashed verticals to ε_c1, ε_c2 and ε_I, with annotations "Z_p2 > Z_p1" and "ε_I > ε_c2 > ε_c1". At ε_I the blue curve collapses steeply to the lowest steady-state level σ_ss1^(v), while the magenta curve jumps upward, grows to a peak σ_p2^(v) and declines to σ_ss2^(v). Right-side labels rank the steady-state stresses σ_ss2 > σ_ss2^(v) > σ_ss1 > σ_ss1^(v); no numeric axis values are printed. The schematic demonstrates that a transient Z_p change at ε_I leaves the Stage-II saturation/steady-state stress below the corresponding constant-condition value.
measured_quantities: Zener-Hollomon parameter Z_p (schematic, no unit printed)

observations.observation: The figure is a schematic true-stress (MPa, vertical axis) versus true-strain (horizontal axis) diagram whose strain axis is divided at ε_I into 'Stage I / Before variation' and 'Stage II / After variation'.

The legend lists four deformation histories: 'Constant Z_p1' (black dashed line), 'Decreasing Z_p from Z_p2 to Z_p1 at ε_I' (blue solid line), 'Constant Z_p2' (purple dashed line) and 'Increasing Z_p from Z_p1 to Z_p2 at ε_I' (magenta solid line).
Text annotations 'Z_p2 > Z_p1' (upper right) and 'ε_I > ε_c2 > ε_c1' (mid-right) are printed inside the plot area.

Two initial stresses are marked on the stress axis at zero strain: σ_01 (lower) and σ_02 (higher); the curves starting from σ_02 form the upper pair (Z_p2 conditions) and those from σ_01 the lower pair (Z_p1 conditions).

Circles mark the critical stresses σ_c1 (lower pair) and σ_c2 (upper pair) together with the peak stress σ_p2 on the upper pair, with dashed verticals linking them to ε_c1, ε_c2 and ε_I on the strain axis.
At ε_I the blue 'Decreasing Z_p from Z_p2 to Z_p1' curve drops almost vertically to the lowest level of the figure, labelled σ_ss1^(v) on the right.
At ε_I the magenta 'Increasing Z_p from Z_p1 to Z_p2' curve jumps upward, grows gradually to a local peak labelled σ_p2^(v) and then declines to a plateau labelled σ_ss2^(v).

The right-hand steady-state labels rank the plateaus from highest to lowest as σ_ss2 > σ_ss2^(v) > σ_ss1 > σ_ss1^(v), i.e. both transiently varied conditions end below their corresponding constant-Z steady-state stresses.

No numeric values are printed on either axis or on any curve; all stresses and strains are given only as symbolic labels (σ_01, σ_02, σ_c1, σ_c2, σ_p2, σ_p2^(v), σ_ss1, σ_ss2, σ_ss1^(v), σ_ss2^(v), ε_c1, ε_c2, ε_I).
The caption states the figure is a 'Schematic diagram of flow stress evolution under varying deformation conditions'.

The citing text states that after transiently decreasing Z_p (increasing T or decreasing strain rate) at ε_I, the flow stress rapidly drops to a level lower than under the corresponding constant deformation conditions.

The citing text states that after transiently increasing Z_p (decreasing T or increasing strain rate) at ε_I, the flow stress gradually grows to a peak lower than that of the constant deformation condition and the subsequent steady-state stress is also lower than under the corresponding constant condition.
The citing text asserts that the saturation stress and steady-state stress in the second stage are severely influenced by the DRX state established in the first stage.
